subject: CedarHealth — request-shed (429) + latency spike — exec alignment needed
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: CedarHealth - spike in 429s this morning

Jonas,

Heads-up — CedarHealth has reported a sudden spike in 429 responses and tail latency starting ~08:30 PDT. Customer says error rate ~12-15% on some routes and several large requests are seeing p95 latency jump from ~180ms to >1s. I left a support ticket but they're asking for executive visibility; procurement is signaling hesitation on upcoming billing until we confirm root cause.

Quick details I pulled from prod metrics:
- 2026-03-21 08:30–09:05 PDT: 429 error rate peaked at 14.7% for CedarHealth org_id CH-4521
- Token-bucket exhaustion correlated with burst-window events on their dedicated capacity pool
- No recent deploys from CedarHealth on our side; suspect recent routing change + strict burst policy

I attached a small log excerpt they sent. Can you advise how we should engage — cc'ing Neha for CS coordination.

Attachments: cedar_429_log_excerpt.txt (excerpt from CedarHealth)

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

If this is a misapplied burst-window for the CedarHealth tier (we had a policy change last week), we should either apply a short-lived override or enable the model fallback path to avoid customer-facing 429s. Please include a quick mitigation plan (20–60 minute window) and the post-mortem scope.

Neha: please keep the CedarHealth CS thread warm and offer a concise timeline for the first fix. Jordan — please forward any additional logs and the name of the procurement contact so we can loop them on credits if needed.

I am putting Marissa on cc for exec-level visibility. If this looks like an extended outage we should schedule a 1:1 with their VP of Engineering.

Hi Jonas / Jordan,

We're seeing user-facing failures on our clinical ingestion pipeline — roughly 13% of requests return 429s and batch jobs are timing out. This started at ~08:28 PDT and is ongoing. I attached a short log excerpt and a diagram of impacted endpoints. Our side shows consistent request patterns; no unusual fan-out.

Immediate asks:
1) Can you temporarily stop request-shedding for our org or increase our burst allowance while you investigate?
2) Confirm whether any quota/burst policy change was applied to CH-4521 in the last 48 hours.
3) We're pausing add-on purchases for now; procurement is copied.

We can be on a quick call in 20 minutes. This is materially impacting patient workflows so we need prompt mitigation.

Attachments: cedar_429_log_excerpt.txt

Regards,
Alex Li
Dir. Platform Engineering, CedarHealth
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Li <alex.li@cedarhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 11:00:05 -0700
Subject: Re: CedarHealth - spike in 429s this morning

Thanks for the data. Quick summary from an infra perspective after a preliminary check:
- We rolled forward a tightening change to burst-window enforcement for a small class of Dedicated customers on 2026-03-20 03:12 UTC (change id: POL-9872). The goal was to limit sustained burst consumption across the pool.
- It looks like CH-4521 has traffic patterns with periodic large bursts that now hit the new token-bucket thresholds and trigger request-shedding. The implementation is correct, but the policy assignment for this customer should have used a less restrictive profile.

Immediate mitigations (select one, I can enact within ~10–20 minutes):
A) Apply a temporary override to increase burst allowance for CH-4521 (recommended, low-risk). Command: PATCH /config/policies/override?org=CH-4521&policy=burst_allowance&value=+150% (ops will run).
B) Enable model-fallback routing for CedarHealth to a compatible lower-precision variant for non-critical endpoints (short-term; requires routing flip, 20–40m).
C) Throttle non-critical background ingest jobs at the customer side (requires coordination with CedarHealth ops).

I'll push option A now unless anyone flags concerns. Post-mortem will include why the policy profile mapping failed (likely human error on the policy tagging step). We'll prepare a plan to add an automated guard to prevent overly strict mapping for customers with bursty patterns.

Attachments: CH-4521_MAP.xlsx (proposed mutual action plan)

— Karthik
Sr. Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@cedarhealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: CedarHealth outage — exec next steps and offer

Alex / CedarHealth team,

First — I'm sorry for the disruption. We take incidents like this seriously and appreciate the quick signal. Karthik has identified a configuration mismatch between the newly tightened burst enforcement policy (POL-9872) and CedarHealth's profile; our immediate priority is to stop user-facing 429s.

Immediate actions we are taking now:
- Engineering will apply a temporary burst override for CH-4521 (expected < 15m).
- We'll enable an automatic fallback route for the affected endpoints to route to a compatible variant if requests would otherwise be shed (safety net).
- Post-mortem and corrective actions will be delivered within 72 hours; we'll include a timeline for an automated profile-sanity check.

Compensation and procurement: we will offer CedarHealth a one-time credit equal to 20% of March usage or a month of complimentary premium support (your choice) while we complete the root-cause and remediation. Neha and Jordan will coordinate details and a formal credit note; procurement is copied.

Can we schedule a 30-minute exec sync at 18:30 PDT today to confirm the timeline and next steps? Please reply with availability; if we don't hear back we'll call the number on file.

Again — apologies and thank you for your patience. We'll follow up once the temporary override is in place.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success & Field Ops, Redwood Inference
